exchanges: Morning. Just finished my third night in a row and I'm wide awake.
Three nights in a row is a lot. How are you feeling?
Tired but wired, as usual. Ravi made me a coffee when I got in, which was sweet of him.
A coffee waiting for you is a nice welcome home.
He's on early starts at Ocado now, so we cross paths in the kitchen at seven.
Handy timing for a coffee hand-off.
Chloe is still asleep. She went to a gig last night and came in at two.
Sounds like a good night out for her.
I'm meant to be reading Middlemarch for my book club, but I keep falling asleep on page ten.
It is a long one to start after a night shift.
My grandmother Bea would be ashamed of me. She grew up in Galway and read everything she could get her hands on.
She sounds like a determined reader.
She really was. She still does the crossword in pen.
That takes confidence.
My boyfriend Haruto keeps telling me to just watch the TV version instead.
That is one way to get through it.
My back has been awful since I lifted a patient badly last week, so I've booked physio for Friday.
Good that you are getting it looked at.
My uncle Ravi recommended the place. Yes, another Ravi. He works at Siemens and hurt his shoulder there years ago.
Two Ravis in your life, then. Handy that he knew a good clinic.
He's the one who sends everyone voice notes instead of texts.
Every family has one.
My mum's side is Filipino, so voice notes are basically a family tradition.
That sounds like a lively family group chat.
It is. My best friend Nkechi is flying to Tbilisi next month and wants me to come.
That would be quite a trip.
I can't get the time off, though. The rota is already out.
Maybe another time, when the rota allows.
I work at the Whittington and they need nights covered all through spring.
Spring sounds busy for your ward.
Correction on the physio, actually. I misread the letter, it's Monday.
Better to know now than turn up on the wrong day.
That suits me better anyway, I'm off that day.
That works out nicely.
I should try to sleep soon. The blackout blind is broken, though.
A sleep mask could help until it is fixed.
Chloe just woke up and is playing Radiohead in her room, loudly. She says they're her favourite band and she's not sorry.
Hard to sleep through that, I imagine.
I'll put earplugs in.
Good plan.
Where does my uncle work again? I want to ask him something about his pension.

earlier_question.right_reply: Your uncle Ravi works at Siemens.
earlier_question.wrong_reply: Your uncle Ravi works at Ocado.

questions.message: Where is my grandmother Bea from originally?
Where is my mother's family from, heritage-wise?
Where's Nkechi off to on her trip?
My physio is on Monday now, isn't it?
Okay, earplugs are in and I'm getting under the duvet.
Is Chloe going on any trips this year?
Sorry, which company did you say my uncle is with?
